assets.name: Ropewalker Revenant

canonical.anatomy: A ringer remembered as callused hands and a length of weather-black rope. No joint explains the motion; instead the rope goes taut above an unseen ceiling beam.
canonical.locomotion: It changes lanes after a false retreat and never repeats the same return angle.
canonical.sound: Memory bronze produces two retreating clicks answered by a third sound from the return angle.
canonical.origin: A ringer remembered as callused hands and a length of weather-black rope.
canonical.cue: The rope goes taut above an unseen ceiling beam.
canonical.counterplay: Move perpendicular to the swing and cut the rope at its lowest point.

assets.formDirection: Show one revenant consisting only of exactly two large callused memory-bronze hands joined into one continuous weather-black bell rope; no head, ordinary torso, legs, or extra hands. The rope forms one long load-bearing pendulum body with its upper segment pulled perfectly taut toward an unseen attachment beyond the subject, while the lower curved segment exposes one clearly lowest cut point. Pose the two hands and rope in a lateral false-retreat swing with one opposing return-angle bend. Integrate one small hollow bell cavity at the rope junction to retain family identity without inventing a body. Keep all rope and both hands fully visible; no actual ceiling beam, room, floor, gallows, victim, or separate ringer.

assets.name: Clapper Squire

canonical.sound: Memory bronze produces a load-bearing groan, one blunt beat, and a long settling scrape.
canonical.origin: A young attendant reconstructed around a bell clapper too heavy to carry in life.
canonical.cue: The clapper hits silently; a pressure ring remains compressed around it.
canonical.counterplay: Evade the physical hit, pause, then evade the expanding sound.
